title: Your Vision-Language-Action Model Already Has Attention Heads For Path Deviation Detection
models: NaVILA (VILA-8B based navigation VLA, 32 layers x 32 heads)
custom PPO obstacle-avoidance policy for recovery
action_head: n/a for manipulation: NaVILA autoregressively generates mid-level language actions ('turn left 30 degrees') executed by a low-level controller
methods: state-machine labeling of trajectory steps as Normal/Anomaly from waypoint progress
attention-head scoring by spatiotemporal alignment (uniformity, peak, diagonal, shift between frames and instruction tokens)
head ranking by Cohen's d of focus sharpness between Normal and Anomaly steps
entropy-ratio monitor over top-K heads with patience threshold
grid search of K, W, P, tau on train split
RL rollback controller in IsaacLab, ROS 2 deployment
question: Do a few attention heads in a frozen navigation VLA carry a signal that detects when the robot has deviated from the instructed path?
key_findings: Three 'navigation heads' out of over a thousand suffice: on R2R Val-Seen, episode detection rate (EDR) 44.6% at false episode rate (FER) 11.7%, step-level F1 78.3%; Val-Unseen EDR 41.9%, FER 9.6%, F1 76.4% (precision 92.5%, recall 65.1%).
Rule-based baselines are weaker: position stagnation EDR 29.6% / FER 5.9% / F1 55.1% on Val-Unseen; action-failure heuristic has negative gap (-4.8%).
Transfer to RxR without retuning: EDR 32.7%, FER 9.7%, F1 50.3% on Val-Unseen.
On the train split, K = 3 heads give EDR 43.9%, FER 9.6%, step precision 92.9%, recall 61.6% (304 N->A scenarios, 2,277 normal and 4,271 anomalous steps).
Ground-truth labels separate on-path (median deviation 0.13-0.16 m) from deviated steps (2.38-2.97 m), Cohen's d > 1.2.
The RL recovery policy reaches 87.3% success in IsaacLab obstacle tests vs 57.4% (APF) and 55.4% (TEB); real-robot rollback on an AgileX Scout is shown qualitatively.

evidence.setting: both (VLN-CE simulation for detection; real robot demonstration)
benchmarks: VLN-CE R2R (1,000 train episodes, Val-Seen 778, Val-Unseen 1,839)
IsaacLab obstacle course for the RL policy (2,048 episodes)
evidence.scale: detection over all validation episodes; 9,000 hyperparameter combinations searched on train
evidence.statistics: partial: Cohen's d for label and head separation; no CIs on detection rates
evidence.baselines: position stagnation and action-failure heuristics; classical local planners (APF, DWA, MPPI, TEB) for the recovery controller

causal_validation: No. The heads are selected and used as a correlational monitor; there is no ablation or patching of the heads to show they implement navigation grounding, and no random-head baseline.
closed_loop: Detection is evaluated on NaVILA's own closed-loop trajectories, but the effect of detection plus rollback on navigation success is not reported quantitatively; real-robot recovery is anecdotal.
limitations_stated: Correcting the physical trajectory without resetting the VLA's internal context can cause repeated errors; replanning or re-prompting is future work.
critique: 'Training-free' is a stretch: heads and thresholds are chosen with ground-truth anomaly labels and a 9,000-configuration grid search on the train split, i.e. supervised selection of a low-dimensional detector.
Detection recall at episode level is modest (about 42-45% of deviated episodes) and the end-to-end benefit (does rollback raise success rate?) is never measured.
No comparison to a learned probe or uncertainty baseline, only to weak kinematic heuristics, so it is unclear whether attention heads are special or any internal signal would do.

Navigation VLA with language-action outputs; relevance to manipulation VLAs with continuous action heads is indirect. Belongs with failure-prediction-from-internals work as much as with attention mechanisms.
code: not released at time of writing (stated 'will be publicly available')
one_line: Entropy of three selected attention heads in the frozen NaVILA navigation VLA flags path deviations (about 42% of deviated episodes at about 10% false alarms), which then triggers an RL rollback controller.
